title: Clean a phone charging port
intro: Cable loose or not charging? Usually it's lint in the port: clear it in 10 minutes.

steps.t: Turn the phone off and unplug the cable.
Shine the torch into the port and look for lint packed at the bottom.
Slide the toothpick in flat along the back wall and gently scrape outwards.
steps.w: Never use pins, needles or paper clips: metal can bend the contacts or short them.

steps.t: Ease the lint out a bit at a time. With USB-C, work around the centre tab and never lever on it.
Give short bursts of compressed air, can upright, about [[3 cm]] from the port.
Look again with the torch: the bottom should be clean, with no clumps.
steps.q: Is the bottom of the port clean?
steps.fix: Go over it gently again with the toothpick. If you see green corrosion or bent pins, stop and take it to a repair shop.

steps.t: Turn the phone on and plug in the cable: it should click and charge without wiggling.
steps.q: Does the cable click in and charge without wiggling?
steps.fix: Try another cable. If it's still loose, the port is worn: take it to a repair shop.

tips: Try another cable first: if that one holds, it's the old cable's plug that's worn.
Don't blow into it: moisture corrodes the contacts. Stick to compressed air.
